input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The separator condition in get_help_spec is inverted: it now uses "; " when no prefix is a slash and " / " when one is, the reverse of the original code.
- rationale: Trigger: any Option whose prefixes include a slash (e.g. /debug/--no-debug or a '/' prefix) with any_prefix_is_slash set. Mechanism: the ternary was changed to `not any_prefix_is_slash`, so the slash-style separator is applied to non-slash options and "; " to slash options. Impact: --help output for such options shows the wrong spelling separators, a visible regression in the help text.
critique: The finding identifies the same inverted ternary on any_prefix_is_slash in get_help_spec. Because of that inversion, ' / ' is used when a slash prefix exists and '; ' otherwise, which garbles the help text. This is the same mechanism as the labeled defect.
